hero.title: Build your event's registration system
hero.lede: A 100% editable registration form, with online payment and complete management of your camp, conference or retreat — all in one place.

comecar.p1: Once your account is created, you sign in to the admin panel with the email and password you set. The panel is organized into cards by area: registrations, finance, form settings and event tools.
comecar.calloutP: Each church is an organization and can have multiple events (the annual camp, a conference, a retreat). Each event has its own form, public page and registrations, isolated from the others.

evento.p1: Under Events, create a new event with a name and identifier (the slug that becomes the public address, for example /e/your-church). Choose whether it will have payment enabled or be free. You can keep registrations closed while you finish setting everything up.

form.p1: In the Form Builder you define which questions the registrant answers. You don't have to start from scratch:
form.pModelo: With an empty form, pick a ready-made template and it creates the base sections and fields for you to adjust:
form.cardAcampamentoP: Personal data, guardian, package (lodging/meals), rides and health.
form.cardCongressoP: Personal data, guardian, registration package and ministry information.
form.cardRetiroP: Personal data, guardian, package, transport and health.
form.pCampos: Organize the form into sections and, within them, fields. Each field has a label, a type and whether it is required. Available types:
form.li1: Short and long text, number, date, email, phone;
form.li2: CPF — ensures a single registration per document;
form.li3: List, single choice and multiple choice (options typed in or pulled from event tables, such as products and price tiers);
form.li4: Consent (LGPD) — acceptance checkbox with text and link;
form.li5: File — the registrant uploads a document (see minor's document).
form.pModulos: Enable the Package module (lodging, meals and transport by category) and the Ride module (offering and requesting seats), when the event calls for it.

produtos.p1: For paid events, register products, group them into package categories and define price tiers with dates and prices. Each registration's amount is calculated automatically from the chosen package, the age-based pricing rules and the event fee.

publicar.p1: Under Form Stage you turn registrations on. The public page lives at /e/your-slug: the registrant logs in, fills out the form (several family members in a single cart) and pays by PIX, card or bank slip. Confirmation is automatic — no need to send a receipt.
publicar.pInst: Each event has an editable institutional landing page (schedule, gallery, partners, how to get there, visit counter) with layout and color templates chosen in the admin, without touching the form.

inscricoes.p1: Under Registrations you see everything in a table, with search, summary cards and export to Excel. You can view details, edit, delete (goes to the trash, with restore) and, for paid registrations, issue a refund.
inscricoes.pAdmin: You can create fields that only the administration fills in after registration (team, internal notes, pastoral family). They appear as extra flagged columns in the table and are included in the export, kept separate from the registrant's answers.
inscricoes.pMenor: Upload a document template per event; the guardian downloads the template in the form and uploads the signed document through the file field. You access each file directly in the registrations table.

ferramentas.cardCheckinP: Attendance by CPF or QR, individual or by order.
ferramentas.cardQuartosP: Distribution of registrants by room, with companions.
ferramentas.cardBoletosP: Installment bank slips and due dates.
ferramentas.cardFaqP: Frequently asked questions in accordions and an optional assistant.
ferramentas.calloutP: Under Roles and Permissions create accounts for your team (secretariat, check-in desk, finance) with access only to what each one needs.

hero.title: Owner runbook
hero.lede: How you run the business: provision and manage churches, get paid via PagarMe split and control overdue payments. A single instance serves all churches as tenants.

painel.p1: The Platform Panel (at /platform) is separate from the churches' admin and only appears to you. Access is granted by an email allowlist: anyone in PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAILS sees the panel; everyone else gets a 403. There you see the totals and the list of all churches.

provisionar.p1: Provisioning is instant — it creates rows in the database, with no manual deploy. Two paths:
provisionar.step1P: The church goes to /comprar, fills in name, identifier and admin data, and the system automatically creates the organization + admin + first event.
provisionar.step2P: You create the organization from the Platform Panel, setting name, identifier, plan and status.
provisionar.calloutP: Today signup already grants immediate access (no confirmation email). The welcome email with credentials is still missing — a planned improvement.

cobranca.p1: You are not a payment facilitator. Money flows through two channels:
cobranca.li1: Registrant → Church: the registration payment lands in the church's own account.
cobranca.li2: Church → You: you keep a percentage, automatically.
cobranca.pSplit: Each church is a recipient in your PagarMe marketplace. On each paid registration, PagarMe performs the split: the church receives (100 − X)% directly and you receive X%. PagarMe holds and settles the funds. In the panel, each organization has its recipient and its platform fee (%).
cobranca.pGratuitos: With no paid registration there is no split, so the church pays you a fixed fee (per event, or a flat amount for unlimited events), with a 14-day trial.
cobranca.calloutDefP: The default %, the free-event fee and the annual plan are edited under Platform pricing, in the owner panel. The fee (%) can be overridden per church. Current defaults: 5%, R$39/event, R$290/year.
cobranca.calloutContP: You are the marketplace of record; PagarMe is the regulated institution. Validate the invoicing of your percentage and your tax classification with an accountant.

inadimplencia.p1: Each organization has a billing status and a due date. The block is staged starting from the due date (or the end of the trial):
inadimplencia.r2Acontece: Full access; email warning of the block.
inadimplencia.r3Acontece: Public page off; admin still gets in.
inadimplencia.p2: A daily job sends the warning/block emails. In the panel, the Billing & overdue section shows the status of all churches (current / due soon / form blocked / admin blocked) and a watch list with the days until the next block.
inadimplencia.p3: To reactivate a church, use the Reinstate button (1 click: back to active and the due date moves forward). Automatic reinstatement — a confirmed payment reactivates the org via webhook — already has the endpoint ready and ships together with real billing on PagarMe.

config.var1: Emails that can see the Platform Panel.
config.var2: Master key of your PagarMe marketplace.
config.var5: Domain used in email links and in the success_url.

hosting.p1: Since it's a single instance serving all churches, the cost is fixed (it doesn't grow per customer) until you need to scale. Components:
hosting.r3Opcao: On the same VPS, or managed
hosting.r5Opcao: S3 / Cloudflare R2 (if migrated off the database)
hosting.p2: Two realistic scenarios at low volume:
hosting.li1: Lean (single self-managed VPS + free FE + email on the free tier): ~US$10–18/month (~R$60–100).
hosting.calloutAtP: Today images and PDFs are stored as BLOBs in MySQL — this bloats the database and raises managed storage cost. Migrating those files to object storage (S3/R2) lowers cost and improves performance.
hosting.calloutEqP: With a fixed cost of ~R$100/month: at an average ticket of R$150 and a 5% fee, ~14 paid registrations/month already cover the infra; or one to two free-event fees. This feeds the pricing definition.
hosting.ref: Values are references (exchange rate ~R$5.50/US$, varies) for sizing — confirm when you sign up.

golive.li1: Recipient onboarding — a bank-details/KYC form creating the recipient on PagarMe.
golive.li2: Checkout via Orders API — migrate PIX/card/bank slip to Orders with split (validate in sandbox).

hero.title: Platform architecture
hero.lede: A multi-tenant instance, a schema-driven form, on top of Spring Boot and React. Overview for dev onboarding and maintenance.

stack.li1: Backend: Spring Boot 3.1.2 · Java 17 · Maven · MySQL · Flyway · Spring Data JPA · Lombok · Spring Security (JWT).
stack.li2: Frontend: React 18 · Vite · react-router · react-bootstrap · react-query · react-toastify · DOMPurify.
stack.li3: Payments: PagarMe API v5 (payment links + Orders; migration to Orders + split in progress).

tenancy.li2: EventResolverInterceptor resolves the slug → Event, populates the EventContext (ThreadLocal) and applies the billing gate.
tenancy.li3: Platform controllers (auth, users, events, /platform) are not event-scoped.
tenancy.li4: On the FE, withEventScope(url) rewrites /x → /e/{slug}/x only for the prefixes in EVENT_SCOPED_PREFIXES.

schema.li1: FormSection / FormField define the form per event; options can come from tables (config.source = products/lots/package_categories).
schema.li2: Modules (Package, Ride) are sections with a moduleType.
schema.li3: EventRegistration stores answers in JSON (answers) and administrative answers in adminAnswers.
schema.calloutP: The generic path (schema-driven, EventRegistration) coexists with the Camper legacy (acampantes tables, specific to IPBV). The IPBV rewrite is the final item on the roadmap.

checkout.p1: GenericCheckoutService creates the charges on PagarMe (Basic auth, sandbox host for sk_test). Revenue model = marketplace + split:
checkout.li1: The church is a recipient under the marketplace; the charge uses the platform's master key.
checkout.li2: PagarmeSplitService builds the percentage split array (church 100 − X, platform X) in payments[].split[].
checkout.li3: Split on the Orders API covers pix/card/bank slip; payment link only splits card — hence the migration.

billing.li2: BillingEnforcementService.levelFor(org) computes NONE / PUBLIC_BLOCKED / ADMIN_BLOCKED (2 and 7 days).
billing.li3: The interceptor returns 402 with billing_blocked: public|admin; staff (role ≠ guest) pass the public-only block.

platform.li1: PlatformController / PlatformService: organizations (CRUD), stats, store FAQ — gated by @platformSecurity.isOwner.
platform.li2: ProvisioningService: creates org + admin + event on signup (14-day trial).
platform.li4: Recent Flyway migrations: V3.73 (organization) → V3.79 (billing status).

hero.title: The registration system built for your church
hero.lede: A personalized form, online payment and complete management of camps, conferences and retreats. No monthly fee weighing on a small church's budget.

porque.h2: Why it's more than a form
porque.p1: There's Sympla (ticket sales) and Google Forms (a form). What doesn't exist is a 100% editable form, focused on the reality of the church, with payment and the automations a Christian event needs.
porque.cardGfP: Here you have payment, packages, user accounts and event control — not just collecting answers.
porque.cardSymplaP: The form is yours, editable field by field, with rides, rooms, teams, wristbands and check-in.

como.step1P: Free, in minutes. You only pay when you create an event.
como.step2P: Start from a ready-made template and adjust fields, packages and the event page.
como.step3P: Share the link and receive registrations and payments straight into the church's account, with automatic confirmation.

precos.p1: Designed to not burden a small church: you pay as you go.
precos.pagoLi1: Service fee added to the registrant
precos.calloutP: A pay-as-you-go model: no mandatory monthly fee, no custody of the church's money. The values (the %, the free-event fee and the annual plan) are set by the owner in the platform panel.

recursos.c1P: Fields, sections and rules your way, with ready-made templates.
recursos.c2P: PIX, card and bank slip with confirmation and no receipt.
recursos.c3P: Offering and requesting seats and the church bus.
recursos.c4P: Lodging and teams organized by the administration.
recursos.c5P: Attendance by QR/CPF on the day of the event.
recursos.c6P: Camp, conferences and retreats in the same account.
recursos.c7P: Institutional landing page with schedule, gallery and map.
recursos.c8P: Registrations in a table, export to Excel and summaries.
